Devin M: Heads up — noticed inconsistency in client-facing errors when routing falls back. Some endpoints return 503 + message 'service unavailable', others return 429 with quota wording. Hard to document in SDKs.
Alex R: Ugh. We need a clear taxonomy: distinguish transient capacity issues (should be 503/service_degraded) vs client-rate/tenant quota (429/quota_exceeded) vs invalid requests (4xx).
Suzanne L: Agree. From Console/Docs POV we want stable strings for consumers to surface: short user-facing message + machine-friendly code + optional dev_hint. Example: `{"code":"quota_exceeded","message":"You exceeded your monthly quota","retry_after":3600}`
Ravi P: +1 but also for routing fallbacks we sometimes degrade to smaller model. That should be a 200 with warnings or a distinct 206? Clients want to know when quality changed.
Alex R: I think 206 is weird for our API semantics. Better: 200 + `warnings` array in body for graceful degradation, and 503 when request didn't complete or was rerouted to a different capacity pool causing failure. Keep HTTP codes aligned to semantics: success vs partial-success vs failure.
Devin M: Proposed minimal mapping: 400 -> invalid_input / auth_error, 401 -> auth, 403 -> forbidden, 404 -> not_found, 429 -> rate_limit or tenant_quota, 503 -> service_unavailable/service_degraded, 500 -> internal_error. Also add machine_code for subtypes, e.g. `service_degraded.cache_miss` or `rate_limit.burst`.
Suzanne L: For console UX we want `user_message` (short, friendly), `developer_message` (more explicit), and `links` to docs for remediation. Example: `{"code":"model_unavailable","user_message":"Temporary model outage — try again in a minute","developer_message":"Model x-neo not available in region us-west-2, fallback attempted","docs":"https://console.redwood.ai/errors#model_unavailable"}`
Ravi P: We should standardize headers too: `Retry-After` when applicable, and a `X-Redwood-Error-Code: quota_exceeded` header to make it easy for proxies and SDKs.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: eng-platform/error-taxonomy -> promoted:staging @ 2026-03-17T14:02:11Z :rocket:
Alex R: Implementation notes: add enum of machine codes in spec, wire SDKs to prefer machine_code over parsing message, and add a small compatibility shim to map historical messages to new codes for 3 months.
Devin M: Action items: 1) Ravi to draft mapping table + header list; 2) Suzanne to draft example UX strings for 5 error classes; 3) Alex to draft spec changes for API; 4) I'll update rollout plan for SDKs. Anyone object to that split?
Suzanne L: No objections. Quick ask — can we make default client-facing strings <100 chars and avoid jargon? :+1:
Ravi P: I'll put the mapping table in a PR by EOD and include sample payloads and curl examples. Example payload for 429: ```json
{
  "code": "quota_exceeded",
  "user_message": "Usage limit reached for this workspace",
  "developer_message": "Tenant 12345 exceeded monthly embed token quota",
  "retry_after": 86400,
  "docs": "https://console.redwood.ai/errors#quota_exceeded"
}
```
Alex R: One more: define `warnings` schema for degraded responses: `"warnings": [{"code":"model_degraded","message":"Using smaller model due to capacity"}]` so SDKs can surface a non-blocking notice.
Devin M: Great. I'll track the PRs. Logging note: include `routing_policy` and `model_variant` in telemetry events for any non-200 responses so we can correlate. Thanks all.
